english.title: Interfere with use / operation of key national infrastructure
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonable excuse and other than wholly or mainly in contemplation or furtherance of a trade dispute, did an act, namely **(..SPECIFY ACT..), which interfered with the use or operation of a key national infrastructure in England and Wales, namely **(..SPECIFY INFRASTRUCTURE..), intending that act to interfere with the use or operation of such infrastructure or being reckless as to whether it would do so
english.legislation: Contrary to section 7(1) and (3) of the Public Order Act 2023.

english.notes:
(i) For the purpose of the offence, a person’s act interferes with the use or operation of key national infrastructure if it prevents the infrastructure from being used or operated to any extent for any of its intended purposes (section 7(4)).
(ii) Key national infrastructure means; road transport infrastructure, rail infrastructure, air transport infrastructure, harbour infrastructure, downstream oil infrastructure, downstream gas infrastructure, onshore oil and gas exploration and production infrastructure, onshore electricity generation infrastructure, or newspaper printing infrastructure (see sections 7(6) and 8).
(iii) A defence is provided by section 7(2) where an individual has a reasonable excuse for doing an act that interferes with the use or operation of any key national infrastructure in England and Wales or, where the interference was done wholly or mainly in contemplation of furtherance of a trade dispute.
(iv) The cases in which infrastructure is prevented from being used or operated for any of its intended purposes include where its use or operation for any of those purposes is significantly delayed.
